blocks.prompt: 8 (a) [printed as 7 (a)] For the function \(f(x) = 2x\) over the interval \([0, 3]\): Find the signed area.
blocks.explanation: The signed area is simply the definite integral \(\int_0^3 f(x)\,dx\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2x\) on \([0, 3]\).
To find: the signed area.
Method: signed area \(= \int_a^b f(x)\,dx\).

Step 1: Integrate
\[\int_0^3 2x\,dx = \left[x^{2}\right]_0^3 = 9 - 0 = 9\]
Why: \(\int 2x\,dx = x^{2}\) by the power rule.

Check:
The region is a triangle with base 3 and height \(f(3) = 6\): \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 6 = 9\).

answer_figure.alt: The line y = 2x from the origin to the point (3, 6); the triangle under it between x = 0 and x = 3 is shaded and lies wholly above the x-axis.
answer_figure.caption: Figure: f(x) = 2x over [0, 3] for Question 8 (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 8 (b) [printed as 7 (b)] For the function \(f(x) = 2x\) over the interval \([0, 3]\): Find the total (physical) area.
blocks.explanation: The total (physical) area is \(\int_0^3 |f(x)|\,dx\). First check whether \(f\) changes sign on the interval.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2x\) on \([0, 3]\).
To find: the total area \(\int_0^3 |2x|\,dx\).
Method: remove the modulus using the sign of \(f\).

Step 1: Sign of \(f\)
For \(0 \le x \le 3\), \(2x \ge 0\), so \(|2x| = 2x\).
Why: the only root \(x = 0\) is the left end, so there is no sign change inside.

Step 2: Integrate
\[\int_0^3 |2x|\,dx = \int_0^3 2x\,dx = 9\]
Why: with the modulus removed, this is the same integral as in part (a).

Check:
Same triangle as in (a): \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 6 = 9\) square units.

blocks.prompt: 8 (c) [printed as 7 (c)] For the function \(f(x) = 2x\) over the interval \([0, 3]\): Explain why they are equal in this case.
blocks.explanation: Signed area and total area differ only when part of the graph is below the axis. So we explain using the sign of \(f\) on \([0, 3]\).
steps:
Given: signed area \(= 9\), total area \(= 9\).
To prove / explain: why the two are equal here.
Method: compare \(\int f\,dx\) with \(\int |f|\,dx\).

Step 1: When are they equal?
\[\int_a^b |f(x)|\,dx = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx \text{ when } f(x) \ge 0\]
Why: if \(f\) is never negative, \(|f(x)| = f(x)\) everywhere on \([a, b]\), so the two integrals are the same integral.

Step 2: Apply to \(f(x) = 2x\)
On \([0, 3]\), \(f(x) = 2x \ge 0\): the whole region lies above the \(x\)-axis (see the figure), so no part is counted negative in the signed area.
Why: only parts below the axis make the signed area smaller than the total area.
blocks.final_answer: The function is non-negative on \([0, 3]\), so there is no negative contribution and the signed area equals the total area (both 9).
